newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House approves leaking oil tank fund changes.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House approves leaking oil tank fund changes.

text.p: The U.S. House passed a bill Wednesday that would give states more say in how they spend money from the federal Leaking Underground Storage Tank (LUST) trust fund.

The bill requires the Environmental Protection Agency to give states at least 85 percent of the money provided by Congress each year from the LUST fund for cleaning up leaking underground oil tanks and preventing future leaks.

The agency over the last 10 years has given states an average of 85 percent of its LUST money, which has ranged from about $45 million to $83 million a year. The bill ensures that funding to states will stay at 85 percent of the total.

The bill allows states to spend the money on enforcing federal leak detection and prevention standards which go into effect next year and which about 70 percent of the 1.2 million tanks nationwide do not meet.

It also lets states use some of the federal funds to administer their tank programs and pay for cleanups when the costs might otherwise force a tank owner out of business and deprive a rural area of an essential gasoline station.
The Senate is expected to start working on similar legislation soon.
The LUST fund was built up with a 0.1 cent per gallon tax on gasoline, which expired in 1995, when the fund had a surplus of $1 billion.
